subject: Pilot economics and next steps — Velocipay discovery readout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Spencer <ava@velocipay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot economics and next steps — Velocipay discovery readout

Hi Ava — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points you called out:
- Token spend volatility on peak business hours (customer chat flows) — current infra costs spike unpredictably.
- p95 latency target of ~150ms for short-form responses (<= 256 tokens).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and audit logs required for procurement.
- Tight pilot budget: you indicated ~USD 25k/month budget for a 4–6 week evaluation.

What we propose for a scoped pilot (to fit budget and demonstrate unit economics):
- Duration: 4 weeks, phased measurement across two stages (Week 1–2: conservative config; Week 3–4: cost/perf optimizations).
- Workload target: ~100k generator calls/day (avg 120 tokens/request).
- Levers we’ll exercise: batching (inference batching to reduce GPU overhead), prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and a medium quantization profile to reduce token unit cost while keeping quality parity.
- Expected tail: we typically see 30–45% token-equivalent reduction combining batching + prefix cache on chat flows like yours; conservatively plan for ~25% in the initial stage.

Estimated economics (conservative, pilot config):
- Baseline token cost (no batching/caching): ~USD 0.015 per 1k tokens -> pilot estimate: $32k/month.
- With conservative batching + prefix cache (expected ~25% reduction): $24k/month (fits your ~$25k guideline).
- Optimized stage (aggressive caching + larger batch windows): potential ~$17–20k/month run rate if production patterns align.

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) I’ll attach a 1‑pager and a short pilot SOW (for scope + acceptance criteria).
2) Security pack (SOC2 + logs) — Marissa will join to confirm the timeline for the evidence pack.
3) If that looks good, we can sign the pilot SOW and aim to start the first measurement week within 7–10 business days.

Do these assumptions match how you’re thinking about budget and success criteria? Any required changes to workload targets or latency constraints?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the attachments and a HubSpot link for signatures.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Ava Spencer <ava@velocipay.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics and next steps — Velocipay discovery readout

Thanks Karthik — clear and helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget: the $25k/month is the upper bound from procurement for a short pilot; procurement will push back if the initial estimate shows >$25k. So the conservative numbers you shared (the $24k/month case) look like the only realistic path. 

2) Latency: the 150ms p95 is a hard preference for the UX team — anything consistently above 200ms will likely be a non-starter. We recognize batching helps cost but may increase tail latency; please include p95 latency tradeoffs for each config in the SOW.

3) Metrics: we need a clear acceptance checklist: p95 <= 150ms on <=256-token responses, token cost <= $X (we’ll set the exact dollar target in the SOW once we see your first conservative projection), and reproducible audit logs for all requests.

4) Security: SOC2 is necessary; we need to confirm whether you can provide a scoped SOC2 package and timeline (our security team requires evidence within 5 business days of contract signing to move procurement).

If you can update the SOW to emphasize the conservative configuration (and include p95 numbers for both conservative and optimized stages), we’ll review internally and loop procurement. Also, can you provide an explicit per-million-token cost projection for each stage (baseline, conservative, optimized)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the one-pager and SOW.

— Ava
Ava Spencer
VP Product, Velocipay
ava@velocipay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Spencer <ava@velocipay.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 18:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics and next steps — Velocipay discovery readout

Thanks both — quick notes from Redwood leadership to address the procurement and latency asks.

- SOC2 & evidence: we can provide a scoped SOC2 packet and the required audit logs. We typically deliver the evidence bundle within 3 business days of a signed pilot SOW for pilots (we’ll flag any redactions up front).

- p95 latency tradeoffs: Karthik is right that batching affects tail latency. For the conservative stage we suggest a small batch window (20–30ms) tuned for p95 <= 150ms; in our internal runs that keeps p95 in the 120–160ms band depending on model size and sequence length. We’ll include p95 projections for both stages in the SOW.

- Per‑million-token cost (illustrative estimates):
  * Baseline (no batching, no cache): $14.50 per 1M tokens
  * Conservative pilot (small batching + prefix cache, ~25% reduction): $10.90 per 1M tokens
  * Optimized (aggressive batching + cache, quantization): $7.50–$9.80 per 1M tokens (range due to model/sequence variance)

Given your $25k/month steering number and the 100k calls/day profile Karthik suggested, the conservative configuration maps to the budget gate — we’ll prioritize demonstrating that outcome in the first two weeks. If procurement needs, we can include a one-time pilot credit to ensure the initial measurement doesn’t block the evaluation. I can sign off on a pilot credit of up to $3k if procurement needs a smoothing mechanism.

I’ll ask our solutions engineer to add a short appendix with the p95 / batching tradeoff table and the security timeline. Karthik — can you share a preferred start date window? Ava — once you confirm, I’ll queue the SOW update and the SOC2 evidence pack for delivery.

Marissa Cole
Head of GTM, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
